name: Tumshuqese
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.source_named: Extinct, fragmentarily attested from manuscripts; sketches (Konow 1935; Emmerick 1989/2009) describe script-based phonology, stress not plausibly recorded

sources.citation: Emmerick, Ronald E. (†). 2024. A Handbook of Khotanese. Completed and edited by M. Maggi, J. S. Sheldon & N. Sims-Williams (Beiträge zur Iranistik 51). Wiesbaden: Reichert. Part II 'Khotanese and Tumshuqese: a survey', §4 Phonology, pp. 284-288 (esp. p. 284).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: open copy online; also held in print at Harvard (Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PK6199.8.Z77 E46 2024)
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PK6199.8.Z77 E46 2024
sources.note: The most recent authoritative survey treating Tumshuqese; p. 284 is the page Peyrot 2025 cites for Tumshuqese ä = ə < unstressed *a and '[ə] in unstressed syllables' -- the one place a Tumshuqese (or joint Khotanese-Tumshuqese) stress remark is known to exist. Part I §1.15-1.16 (open sample, saved) already gives the explicit Khotanese rule.

sources.citation: Kim, Ronald I. 2023 [2025]. Review of Emmerick, A Handbook of Khotanese (2024). Abstracta Iranica. doi:10.4000/15h3l.
sources.note: States Part II of the Handbook is 'based on the original draft of Emmerick's chapter in The Iranian Languages' (Routledge 2009) and covers scripts, orthography, phonology, morphology, syntax; no stress detail.

sources.citation: Ogihara Hirotoshi. 2021. Miscellany on the Tumshuqese documents: Part II. Pis'mennye pamjatniki Vostoka 18(3): 148-159. doi:10.17816/wmo77877 (open).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Never mentions stress/accent. Notes 'vowel reduction in the penultimate syllable' (dṛd1ane > dṛd1ne, lāẓid1ane > lāẓid1ne, dauwarsañyo > dauwarsño; pp. 152-153, fn. 11, 13) without linking it to accent.

sources.citation: Hitch, Douglas. 2016. The Old Khotanese Metanalysis. PhD dissertation, Harvard University.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Tumshuqese mentioned only for script features and one consonant correspondence; its stress discussion (§3.3.2.1.5) concerns Old Khotanese only.

sources.citation: Encyclopaedia Iranica online (site search for 'Tumshuqese' via reader proxy).
sources.note: No dedicated Tumshuqese-language article exists; only 'BUDDHISM iii. Buddhist literature in Khotanese and Tumshuqese' and 'IRAN vi(2) Documentation' mention the language.

sources.citation: Ogihara Hirotoshi. 2025. A new look at ownership clauses in Tumshukese sale contracts. In Ching & Peyrot (eds.), Text, Script and Language in Bactria and Serindia (BzI 55), 253-273. Wiesbaden: Reichert.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Philology of contracts; script remarks only; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Peyrot, Michaël. 2025. On the so-called "Fremdvokal" ä in Tocharian and Khotanese and its origins. In Ching Chao-jung & Michaël Peyrot (eds.), Text, Script and Language in Bactria and Serindia (Beiträge zur Iranistik 55), 275-296. Wiesbaden: Reichert. Open Access, doi:10.29091/9783752003635.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: §5 'ä in Tumšuqese Brāhmī', p. 282 (PDF p. 293): second-hand only -- 'According to Maue & Sims-Williams (2024: 37), the value of <ä> in Tumšuqese is ə.. According to Emmerick (2024: 284), it notes ə for original unstressed *a', fn. 12 quoting Emmerick 2024: 284 'Other vowels may have had an allophone [ə] in unstressed syllables'. Implies unstressed syllables existed; says nothing about WHERE stress fell. §7 p. 285 (Khotanese) 'reduction of unstressed a to ä as in hvatäna-'.
